page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n2.medium is an entry-level virtual server instance within the shared family, configured with a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads via Intel Hyper-Threading, clocked at 2.5 GHz. The CPU architecture is x86_64, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. The processor incorporates 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache. It supports instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512 Foundation, AES, and FMA. Memory capacity is 8.0 GB, which equals 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or bundled GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results place the computational and memory capabilities of ecs.n2.medium in the lower tiers across standardized tests. In stress-ng, it achieved a single-core score of 1,107.09 and a multi-core score of 2,193.58. PassMark evaluations yielded a CPU score of 2,641.62 and a memory score of 1,211.79. Data compression speeds reached 18.98 GB/sec for single-threaded gzip and 6.77 GB/sec for single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Uncached 256MB memory throughput achieved 16.61 GB/sec for reads and 14.38 GB/sec for writes, while small cached blocks reached 157.12 GB/sec. Application testing delivered 2.49 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and a static web serving throughput of 1.69 GB/sec.

The qualitative trade-off of this configuration is centered around resource density and cost efficiency for low-footprint services. With only two execution threads and no local ephemeral storage, high-throughput I/O or heavy mathematical compute is constrained. However, the 8 GB memory pool provides sufficient headroom for light background tasks, non-critical web serving, development environments, and low-traffic caching layers that do not require intense core parallelization.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n2.medium is a general-purpose virtual machine featuring 2 vCPUs from a single physical core (Intel Xeon 8269CY, 2.5 GHz) and 8.0 GB of memory. Operating on the x86_64 architecture with KVM virtualization, it includes 35 MB L3 cache alongside AVX-512 and AES instructions. The configuration does not feature dedicated GPUs or onboard local storage. In benchmark assessments, it produced 1,107.09 in stress-ng single-core and 2,193.58 in multi-core compute, with uncached memory read bandwidth of 16.61 GB/sec and Redis SET throughput of 2.49 million operations per second. While throughput across intensive compute and database benchmarks falls into lower industry tiers, the 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio provides a balanced, low-footprint environment well-aligned with entry-level web serving, lightweight microservices, and development testing.
